## thesis_being_attacked

PRISM Diagnostics' Quantum-2 platform launch + installed-base consumables compounding will drive FY28 EPS to $5.65 and justify a re-rating to 28×, generating ~41% return over 3 years.

## outcome

partial — the strongest counter weakened the FY28 base by ~$0.10 and was incorporated into the paper's model. Paper proceeds with appendix disclosure.

## strongest_counter

**Description:** historical consumables-per-platform trajectory in mature platform generations shows deceleration as menu coverage saturates. PRSM's current flagship (G-IV) reached 47 approved assays by FY25, vs. 31 at the same platform-age for the prior generation (G-III). G-III's per-platform consumables CAGR decelerated by ~0.4pp in years 6–7 of its life cycle as menu saturated.

**Evidence:**

- PRSM FY22 10-K Item 7, p.43 (G-III generation per-platform trajectory)
- PRSM FY25 10-K Item 7, p.51 (G-IV current trajectory)
- Internal computation: G-III per-platform CAGR yr 1-5 = 4.7%, yr 6-7 = 4.3% (-0.4pp)

**Why it invalidates:**

If G-IV decelerates analogously in FY27 (its 6th year of consumables ramp), the base-case FY28 consumables per platform of $44.5K could be $43.7K instead. That moves FY28 consumables revenue $760M → $748M and FY28 EPS to approximately $5.55 (-$0.10 vs. paper's $5.65). At target multiple 28×, target price = $155 instead of $158, IRR drops to ~11.8% — still above the 10% threshold.

**Weakness:**

The G-III deceleration was 0.4pp; G-IV may not decelerate analogously because Quantum-2 (the new platform) introduces a *new* menu vector that opens space for fresh consumables introductions, partially offsetting menu saturation on G-IV.
